correctness.rationale: Base-r even/odd digit separation proves unique additive representation. The three-way induction for D(x)=lambda*x-a(x)b(x), and strengthened bounds on x in A and x in B, closes via x=Q*t+s, with t positive belonging to at most one set (except zero handled separately). Exact displayed lower bounds use rv>lambda or u>=r>lambda. An explicit sequence j_k=2r^(k-1)-1 gives a(x_k)=r^k, b(x_k)=2r^(k-1) and asymptotic ratio lambda=2(r+1)/(r+2). Independently enumerated complete Q^3 finite ranges for r=2..5 and checked all strengthened inequalities. Finite checks are corroboration of the all-radix inductive proof, not its basis.
